description: We are building an Edge-AI Earth system trend detector using NASA satellite telemetry. Our solution pairs multi-variable statistical testing (Mann-Kendall & Granger Causality) with an 8-bit quantized flight-computer simulator to filter seasonal weather noise and isolate significant regional climate and pollution shifts.
summary: Orbital Trend Detective is a hybrid Earth-system analytics and CubeSat edge-AI engine built by Team Fluid Edge Intelligence for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge (Be An Earth System Trend Detective!). Analyzing 16 years (2010–2026, 189 monthly orbital cycles) of multi-satellite telemetry from NASA Giovanni—combining MODIS Aerosol Optical Depth (MOD08_M3 v6.1), MERRA-2 Land Surface Temperature (M2TMNXLND v5.12.4), and GPM IMERG Precipitation (GPM_3IMERGM v07)—our platform separates true multi-year climate trends from repeating seasonal weather and monsoon rain washout. By pairing Seasonal-Trend Decomposition (STL), Mann-Kendall rank tests, and Granger Causality F-tests with an 8-bit integer (INT8) quantized neural anomaly detector (0.28 KB memory footprint, ~0.01 ms pass latency), our system uncovers localized compound heat-and-aerosol anomalies in Hyderabad and the Amazon Basin that planetary averages dilute, while reducing CubeSat downlink bandwidth requirements by 96.3% to 98.4%.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Orbital Trend Detective is a hybrid Earth-system analytics and CubeSat edge-AI flight-computer simulator built by Team Fluid Edge Intelligence. Analyzing 16 years (2010–2026, 189 monthly orbital cycles) of multi-satellite telemetry from NASA Giovanni—combining MODIS Aerosol Optical Depth (MOD08_M3 v6.1), MERRA-2 Land Surface Temperature (M2TMNXLND v5.12.4), and GPM IMERG Precipitation (GPM_3IMERGM v07)—our platform solves two core bottlenecks in Earth observation:

1. Seasonal & Monsoon Weather Subtraction: Applies Seasonal-Trend Decomposition using LOESS (STL) to strip 12-month seasonal cycles and subtracts regression-adjusted GPM rainfall anomalies to isolate genuine multi-year emission and warming trends from monsoon aerosol washout.

2. Econometric Trend & Causation Engine: Enforces stationarity via Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) tests, proves non-parametric trend significance using Mann-Kendall rank tests, and runs multi-lag Granger Causality F-tests (1–6 months) across Global Planetary (-180° to +180°), Greater Hyderabad Airshed (78°E–79°E, 17°N–18°N), and Amazon Basin (63°W–61°W, 4°S–2°S) corridors.

3. On-Board INT8 CubeSat Anomaly Detector: Quantizes a 3-sensor neural anomaly detector into 8-bit signed integers (0.28 KB memory footprint, 75% smaller than FP32), running in 0.0066–0.0106 ms per orbital pass to transmit only top-decile compound heat-and-aerosol anomalies.

BENEFITS & REAL-WORLD IMPACT

• Faster Public Health Warnings: On-board anomaly alerts deliver compound heat-and-smog warnings in minutes instead of waiting hours or days for full ground-station data dumps.

• Verified Municipal Climate Policy: Subtracting monsoon rain washout gives local pollution boards statistical proof of true emission trends rather than temporary weather relief.

• Lower-Cost CubeSat Missions: Cutting downlink bandwidth by 96.3% to 98.4% enables universities and emerging space programs to monitor regional climate health using smaller, lower-power radios.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & CREATIVITY

• Software & Stack: Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Statsmodels, Scikit-learn, and Plotly (open-source under MIT License, deployed via GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud).

• Target Flight Hardware & Portability: Designed for low-power CubeSat microcontrollers (such as ARM Cortex-M and STM32 flight boards). Because the quantized model relies purely on INT8 integer matrix math (0.28 KB), its weights export directly into dependency-free C++ header arrays with zero Python runtime required in orbit.

• Creativity & Key Factors Considered: Rather than building a passive chart viewer, we bridged ground climate econometrics with sub-kilobyte spacecraft edge AI—accounting for regional dilution (where global averages hide Hyderabad's 5/189 and the Amazon's 7/189 extreme compound passes), orbital radio bandwidth limits, and false-positive rain-washout traps.

TEAM ROLES (TEAM FLUID EDGE INTELLIGENCE)

• Parikshith: System architecture, 2010–2026 NASA Giovanni telemetry acquisition, STL + GPM noise-subtraction and Granger Causality modeling, and 0.28 KB INT8 CubeSat edge-AI design.

• Varun: Public GitHub repository management, dependency configuration, Streamlit Community Cloud deployment, and presentation packaging.
